intent.quote: B. I guess the CLI / lib can be re-used from pi-agent-factory?
intent.readback: plumb works in any repository and for any coding agent: one host-neutral core does the work, and each host gets a thin adapter that installs only that host's own things. The Claude Code plugin installs only Claude Code's command, skills, checks and panels, and the Codex, Pi and Hermes adapters likewise install only their own. Adopting a repository is one plain request that changes nothing the second time, and where plumb is not adopted it stays silent apart from one line. plumb is built with plumb.
will: One host-neutral core that every coding agent's adapter feeds, so the same session gives the same agent context, owner lines and block on every host, with a no-hook fallback the agent runs.
A Claude Code plugin that carries its own copy of plumb and installs only Claude Code's command, skills, background checks and panels.
Thin adapters for Codex, Pi and Hermes, each writing only its own host's files, keeping your own entries and removing only plumb's.
A read-only MCP server any host can add.

Adoption of any repository on a plain request or /plumb init, idempotent, with one line and nothing else where plumb is not adopted; projects set up the old way keep working and move to the plugin on request.
plumb developed with plumb: its own repository adopted like any other, its commits naming the requirement they serve.
wont: Install anything for one host when plumb is set up for another, or copy Claude Code's command, skills or checks into a project.
Run the project's own development setup of plumb from the plugin.
Ask you to type a shell or install command, or a record id.
Claim a host's adapter is active when it has only written its files.
Depend on pi-agent-factory at run time.
assumptions: Assumed: 'each host installs only its own things' means setting plumb up for one host writes nothing for any other host, and the Claude Code plugin writes nothing of Claude Code's into a project either (SR-083's rule).

Assumed: SR-015 (proposed: a per-project installer writes Claude Code's hooks, status line, deny rules, skill and CLAUDE.md block) is settled against SR-082 (confirmed): the plugin sets plumb up, and the per-project installer of Claude Code things retires.

Assumed: the owner reaches adoption and host set-up in plain words or /plumb init (no id); the agent runs any shell step (P2). 'plumb hosts install <host>' and 'plumb turn start' stay as the agent's steps.

Assumed: the per-host 'plumb approve exits 3' examples become one example about any approval-writing or answer-posting step the agent runs, since there is no approval command (P2, P3); the guard itself belongs to P3's requirement, the adapter only sets its host's session marker.

Assumed: the per-host status examples drop 'owner-only commands require an interactive terminal' (P2: the owner runs no terminal commands) and keep the missing marker, where prompts come from and the count of approvals resting on a self-recorded message.
Assumed: SR-083's 'full test run at push' is dropped: verification is by targeted covering tests and a full run only for a named reason (P10); git's push check remains, its content belongs to P10.
Assumed: SR-053's clause on typed owner commands (undo, go, approve) is dropped: there is no approval command (P3) and the owner's plain-word commands belong to P2's requirement.
Assumed: 'builds itself with itself' (INT-009) is an example under adoption, not a requirement of its own; no old record in these clusters states it.
Assumed: the anchors SR-123 and SR-109 name no feature; the plugin and adoption requirements take FEAT-007 (SR-082, SR-083, SR-084), the core, adapter and MCP requirements take FEAT-004.

Assumed: the event-mapping examples of SR-055, SR-056 and SR-100 are carried under the core requirement, while those records are superseded by the adapter requirement that carries their install behaviour.

requirements.title: The Claude Code plugin installs only Claude Code's things and runs its own copy of plumb
requirements.statement: plumb's repository offers plumb as a Claude Code plugin that carries a ready-built copy of plumb and installs only Claude Code's things: the /plumb command, plumb's skills, its background checks and its in-app panels. Everything it runs uses plumb's own private copy of its tools, kept per user and plugin version, never the project's setup; the copy is set up in the background, and only an adopted project shows a line about it. The shipped bundle holds only what runs, no test file; the command guard starts no Python for a command that does not concern plumb; on Windows the launcher uses Git for Windows' sh.exe when cmd.exe has no sh on its PATH.

examples.given: a machine with Claude Code and uv but no plumb anywhere
examples.when: the owner adds plumb's plugin list and installs the plumb plugin with Claude Code's plugin commands, then opens a session in any project
examples.then: /plumb, the plumb skills and the background checks are available, and nothing was written into that project

examples.then: nothing for Codex, Pi or Hermes was written: no AGENTS.md block, no .codex entry, no Pi extension, no Hermes plugin

examples.then: it is set up once in the background, the owner sees one plain line saying plumb is getting ready, and checks that cannot run yet stay silent; in a project not adopted no such line appears

examples.given: setting up plumb's private copy fails (no Python 3.12 or later, or the install step fails)
examples.then: the owner sees one plain line saying plumb could not get ready and why, no half-built copy is left and the next session tries again

examples.then: both pass, and the validation lists what the in-app panels respond to

proof.plan: Recommended: in a clean user profile with Claude Code and uv, the agent installs the plugin from plumb's plugin list, opens a session in a scratch git repository and types /plumb; the owner sees /plumb answer, git status of the scratch repository showing no change, and no Codex, Pi or Hermes file present. The owner decides whether this live walk or a recording of it is the proof.

requirements.title: plumb adopts a repository once, on a plain request, and stays silent where it is not adopted
requirements.statement: On a plain request or /plumb init, plumb adopts the repository: its record folder with settings, git's checks at commit, merge and push each calling one plumb launcher in the user's folder, and a way for git to merge plumb's records; adopting again changes nothing. A repository not adopted gets one line per session suggesting adoption and nothing else. plumb's own repository is adopted the same way.

examples.given: a fresh git project and the plugin installed
examples.when: the owner says "set up plumb here" or types /plumb init
examples.then: plumb's record folder exists, git's checks at commit, merge and push each call plumb's launcher, git knows how to merge plumb's records, and the project's Claude Code settings are unchanged

examples.given: a git repository without .plumb/
examples.then: the record directories, config, claims, ignore and attributes files and empty logs are created

examples.given: an adopted repository
examples.then: plumb says it is already adopted and changes nothing

examples.given: the adopted project
examples.then: the commit check is installed and calls plumb's launcher; what it holds is P11's

examples.given: a project without plumb's record folder
examples.when: a session starts and the owner sends three messages that edit files
examples.then: the only plumb output of the session is the one line "/plumb init to adopt this repository", and plumb writes nothing

examples.given: a project without plumb's record folder
examples.when: plumb's checks run after a message, an edit and an answer
examples.then: each finishes within a tenth of a second without starting plumb itself

examples.given: an adopted project
examples.then: the merge-time check is installed and calls plumb's launcher, running no test; what it holds is P11's

examples.given: plumb's own repository with the plugin installed
examples.then: a commit whose trailer names no requirement it serves is held by the commit check, as in any adopted repository

proof.plan: Recommended: in a live session the owner says "set up plumb here" in a scratch git repository and sees the record folder and git's checks appear with the project's Claude Code settings unchanged; asks again and sees nothing change; then opens a session in a second, unadopted repository and sees only the one adoption line. The owner decides whether this walk is the proof.

requirements.title: A project set up the old way keeps working, and moves to the plugin on request
requirements.statement: In a project where plumb's settings, command and skills were copied in, plumb's checks run once per turn whether or not the plugin is also active, under the version 2 rules. Asked to move to the plugin, plumb removes only what it wrote and left unchanged, points git's checks at its launcher, and names what the owner changed and it kept.

examples.given: a project set up the old way, with the plugin also installed
examples.then: each of plumb's checks runs once and the owner sees one summary

examples.given: that project, where the owner edited the copied /plumb command and added a Claude Code setting of their own
examples.when: the owner says "move plumb to the plugin"
examples.then: plumb's own settings and the unchanged copied skills are removed, the edited command and the owner's own setting stay and are named, and git's checks call plumb's launcher

examples.given: a project set up the old way, on a machine without the plugin (a teammate, a build server)
examples.then: the project's own copied checks run plumb once each, with the version 2 behaviour the plugin's would have: no approval command, no card, questions only

proof.plan: Recommended: in a scratch project set up the old way with one edited copied file, the owner says "move plumb to the plugin" and sees plumb's own copies go, the edited file stay and be named, and a turn afterwards show one summary. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

requirements.title: One host-neutral core gives every host the same turn, with a no-hook fallback
requirements.statement: Every host's adapter turns its events into the core's turn events and shows the core's turn output: agent context, owner lines, at most one block and the status. The same scripted session gives the same output on Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Hermes. A host without lifecycle hooks gets the same through plumb turn start and plumb turn end, which the agent runs. Events reach only the project the adapter was installed in.

examples.given: a scripted session of session start, a prompt naming SR-001, an edit and a stop
examples.when: it is driven with host claude-code, codex, pi and hermes
examples.then: agent_context, owner_lines and block are identical across hosts

examples.given: a host with no lifecycle hooks
examples.when: the agent runs plumb turn start with the prompt and plumb turn end
examples.then: the prompt digest is logged, the delta and the summary are printed and both exit 0

examples.given: a host whose prompts reach plumb only through plumb turn start
examples.when: the agent runs plumb turn start with the owner's message
examples.then: the prompt log entry says via turn, not hook, so an approval resting on that message is labelled "self-recorded message"; a host's own prompt hook logs via hook

examples.given: a repository whose session brief reaches the watchdog's limit
examples.when: the agent runs plumb turn start, on the first turn or a later one, with the message on stdin or in --prompt-file
examples.then: the owner's message is logged (via: turn) even when the brief is cut by the watchdog, and later turns do not repeat the brief

proof.plan: Recommended: the agent drives one scripted session through each of the four hosts and shows the owner the four agent contexts, owner lines and blocks side by side, identical, then runs the same turn with plumb turn start and end on a host without hooks. The owner decides whether this side-by-side is the proof or wants a live session on a second host.

requirements.title: Codex, Pi and Hermes each get a thin adapter that installs only that host's own things
requirements.statement: Asked to set plumb up for Codex, Pi or Hermes, plumb writes only that host's adapter: Codex's AGENTS block and hooks, Pi's extension, Hermes's plugin and namespaced skills, each with the /plumb command where the host has one and its session marker where it can be set. Installing twice changes nothing, the owner's own entries are kept, uninstalling removes only plumb's, and status reports what is installed without claiming it is active. Each adapter binds events to the project it was installed in, ignores child sessions, gives the brief once, sends a block at most once, and records a summary that never reached the owner as unseen.

examples.when: plumb's Codex adapter is installed twice
examples.then: the owner's text is unchanged and one plumb block exists

examples.given: plumb's Codex adapter installed
examples.then: only plumb's entries are removed

proof.plan: Recommended: in a scratch repository holding the owner's own AGENTS.md and Hermes config, the agent sets plumb up for Codex, then Pi, then Hermes, twice each, and shows the owner the diff after each: only that host's files changed, the owner's text intact, and an uninstall diff removing only plumb's entries. The owner decides whether these diffs or a live session in one of those hosts is the proof.

requirements.title: The Hermes adapter writes plumb's block into the one context file Hermes reads
requirements.statement: Hermes reads one context file, so the Hermes adapter writes plumb's instruction block where Hermes looks: the first of .hermes.md and HERMES.md that exists, when it is nonempty; otherwise the first nonempty of AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.md included although it is Claude Code's file. An empty file is left unchanged, and no AGENTS file is created to shadow another. Uninstalling keeps a block in a file another host may share and explains why.

examples.given: only a nonempty CLAUDE.md exists
examples.then: CLAUDE.md receives the block with its text retained, and no AGENTS file is created

examples.given: a nonempty .hermes.md and a nonempty CLAUDE.md
examples.then: .hermes.md receives the block and CLAUDE.md is unchanged

examples.given: an empty .hermes.md and a nonempty CLAUDE.md
examples.then: CLAUDE.md is selected and the empty Hermes file remains unchanged

examples.given: an empty .hermes.md and a nonempty HERMES.md
examples.then: HERMES.md and the empty .hermes.md are left untouched, and the block goes to the first nonempty of AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md

examples.given: nonempty AGENTS.override.md and AGENTS.md exist
examples.then: only AGENTS.override.md receives the block

examples.given: the Claude context file has a plumb block
examples.then: the block is kept and its shared or unknown ownership is explained

proof.plan: Recommended: in a scratch repository holding only a nonempty CLAUDE.md, the agent sets plumb up for Hermes and shows the owner the diff: the block added to CLAUDE.md, no AGENTS.md created. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

requirements.title: plumb's MCP server is read-only
requirements.statement: plumb's MCP server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio with the standard library only and exposes six read-only tools (brief, relevant, show, explain, impact, drift) returning what plumb shows the agent; it has no write tool and leaves .plumb outside its cache unchanged. Adding it to a host writes plumb's entry once into that host's config and keeps the owner's servers.

examples.given: a client sends initialize then tools/list
examples.then: the six tools are listed, each with readOnlyHint true, and nothing else

examples.given: a repository with records and logs
examples.then: every file under .plumb outside cache is byte-identical afterwards

examples.given: a client calls an unknown method
examples.then: it returns JSON-RPC error -32601

examples.given: a .mcp.json, .codex/config.toml or Hermes config.yaml with the owner's own servers
examples.when: plumb's MCP entry is added for that host twice and then removed
examples.then: plumb's entry is written once and removed, and the owner's servers are untouched

proof.plan: Recommended: the agent adds plumb's MCP server to a host, lists its tools there (six, all read-only), calls each, and shows the owner that .plumb outside the cache is unchanged and the owner's other servers are still listed. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

retired_decisions.why: matters false and an implementation choice; its rule (the plugin carries a ready-built plumb checked against the source and sets up a private copy per user and plugin version, called through one launcher) is stated by the plugin requirement
